messages.subject: How to get p.Ia value
parts:
Dear Zhian

I tried to use function
 poppr(dataset, sample = 999) or 
poppr(dataset) 
res <- pair.ia(dataset, sample = 999) to try to get p.Ia value
but then the programming runs extremly slowly. Do you have a better solution to get this p value? 

Thank you very much.

Best regards
Ying

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] How to get p.Ia value
parts:
All of these methods use randomizations to obtain the p-value. These randomizations must shuffle the data and recompute the index, and thus can be time intensive, especially if you have a large data set. I'm afraid that's the only way a p-value for the index of association is calculated.

pair.ia will run especially slow because it calculates the index and a p-value for each locus separately.

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] How to get p.Ia value
parts:
Hi Ying,

Yes, if you set sample = 99, then it will randomize the data and recalculate the index 99 times. With any randomization procedure, more samples will give you a more precise p-value (but that also depends on your sample size).

Using set.seed(1000) means that your sampling will be reproducible.

Best,

Zhian
